 The Hon'Ble Smt.Justice K. Sujana
 Criminal Petition No.3719 of 2023
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by the petitioners/accused Nos. 2 and 3 to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.488 of 2023 on the file of learned I Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-XII Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally,
Cyberabad, for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").
2.

entities.text:
Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-XII Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally,
Cyberabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that the de facto complainant was working as Branch Manager,
Kukatpally Branch the Quelitek Pharma is a partnership Firm established in the year 2006 by A-1 and A-2 as partners and A-3 and A-4 stood as guarantors was engaged in the business activity of manufacturing of pellets which are used for drug administration through capsules.

In the year 2009,
the guarantors of the said firm requested the bank for various loans/facilities and various credit facilities.
The total amount of loan was sanctioned for Rs.498.59 lakhs for various facilities and the total amount outstanding as on 26.12.2019 is Rs. 265.83 lakhs.

On verification came to know that one of the link document vide document No.879 of2006, dated 18.01.2006 which is duly registered with Sub Registrar Office is found to be fabricated document, stamp papers also different and SRO signature is also not tallying.

Therefore, bank is not in a position to enforce its security and the petitioners in collusion with guarantor defrauded the bank by submitting the fake title deed for the loan to a tune of Rs.265.83 lakhs plus interest.

Based on the complaint a case was registered vide Crime No.01 of 2020 before Kukatpally Police and after completion of investigation, a charge sheet was filed vide C.C.No.488 of 2023 on the file of learned I Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-XII Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally, Cyberabad.

entities.text: I Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-XII Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally, Cyberabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Heard Sri B. Vijay Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri S. Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 and Sri M.V.Ramana, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the material on record.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that there are no fabricated documents and Police after investigation found that there is no forgery and, sections 406 and 420 of IPC are not maintainable.

In this regard, he relied on the Judgment in the case of Binod Kumar and others v.
State of Bihar and another 1, in the case of Prof.R.K.Vijayasarathy and another v. Sudha Seetharam and another 2 and in the case of Rekha Jain and another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and others 3 and prayed the Court to allow the criminal petition by quashing the proceedings against the petitioners.
5.

As such,

sentences.text: Having regard to the rival submissions made by both the learned counsel and having gone through the material available on record, it is noticed that originally criminal case registered for the offences under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 406 of IPC, wherein allegation is that document No.879 of 2006 is a fabricated document which is given as security to respondent bank while availing loan.
The averments in the charge sheet shows that police investigated about the genuinity of document and found that the above document is genuine.
The executors of the said document did not dispute the execution and nobody else claimed property under the said document.
Further, Revenue Divisional Officer of the Ranga Reddy East accepted the title of said land and granted permission for conversion of land.
Thus, the title of Gopalakrishna is not in dispute and land is available on the ground.
In spite of clarification, A-1 to A-3 have submitted another property with equal value covered by valid documents as substitute mortgage for loan.
Therefore, police while filing charge sheet deleted the offences under Sections 468 and 471 of IPC and filed for the offences under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
When the petitioners given other property as security equally valued and the bank accepted the same, maintaining sections 406 and 420 of IPC does not arise.

Further the Apex Court in the case of Binod Kumar (supra 1), Prof.R.K.Vijayasarathy (supra 2) and Rekha Jain (supra 3) observed that no case of criminal breach of trust or dishonest intention of inducement is made out and the essential ingredients of Sections 406 and 420 of IPC are missing, as such, the prosecution of the petitioners under Sections 406 and 420 are liable to be quashed.

Since the petitioners given other property as security equally valued and the bank accepted the same, the continuation of the proceedings against the petitioners are abuse of process of law and the petition is liable to be allowed.

7. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 in C.C.No.488 of 2023 on the file of learned I Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum- XII Metropolitan Magistrate at Kukatpally, Cyberabad, are hereby quashed.
